script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

Title: Unraveling

INT. UNIVERSITY LAB - DAY

A bright, sterile room filled with scientists huddled around monitors, working in silence.

PROF. RUSSEL (60s, disheveled, passionate), a renowned geneticist, stands at the front of the room.

PROF. RUSSEL
Ladies and gentlemen, today we will unveil the culmination of years of research. Our team has unlocked the key to understanding the human genome. But as we delve deeper, we're uncovering secrets that challenge our very identities.

INT. PROF. RUSSEL'S OFFICE - LATER

Prof. Russel sits alone, staring at a large genome map on his wall. He looks troubled.

A KNOCK.

Prof. Russel (O.S.)
Enter.

ASSISTANT JEN (30s, eager, professional) enters, holding a stack of files.

ASSISTANT JEN
Professor, we have some significant findings on the latest genome sequences.

Prof. Russel (absently)
Yes, yes, please.

ASSISTANT JEN
(putting files down)
These sequences reveal an unexpected genetic mutation. It's present in approximately 1% of the population, and it's affecting their facial features and cognitive abilities.

Prof. Russel, alarmed, looks up from his paperwork.

PROF. RUSSEL
(sternly)
What do you mean "cognitive abilities"?

ASSISTANT JEN
Well, it's not quite clear yet, but it seems to impact their learning and memory skills.

Prof. Russel stands up, pacing around the room.

PROF. RUSSEL
We need to investigate this further. We must identify those affected and provide them with the necessary resources and support.

INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - NIGHT

Prof. Russel spends hours poring over genetic research, his eyes bloodshot and exhausted.

Suddenly, he spots a familiar face in an old photo. It's his estranged sister, who he hasn't seen in decades.

Prof. Russel (whispering to himself)
Could she be one of the carriers?

INT. PROF. RUSSEL'S SISTER'S APARTMENT - DAY

Prof. Russel stands nervously outside his sister's apartment. He takes a deep breath and knocks.

SIS. MARTHA (40s, warm, surprised) answers the door. They share an emotional reunion.

SIS. MARTHA
(tearfully)
I can't believe it's really you!

They sit down to catch up, but the conversation quickly turns to the genetic research.

SIS. MARTHA
(confused)
What are you doing here, Russ?

PROF. RUSSEL
(hesitantly)
I came to ask you a question. I believe you might have this genetic mutation.

Sis. Martha's expression turns to shock and disbelief.

SIS. MARTHA
(defensively)
What makes you think that?

PROF. RUSSEL
Your facial features, for one. And your memory lapses.

Sis. Martha looks down, her eyes welling up with tears.

SIS. MARTHA
(sighing)
I've had a feeling something was off for a while now. I've tried to ignore it, but I can't deny it any longer.

PROF. RUSSEL
We need to get you tested as soon as possible. There's a support group for those with this mutation, and they can provide you with valuable information and resources.

Sis. Martha nods in agreement.

INT. UNIVERSITY LAB - DAY

Prof. Russel and his team work tirelessly to identify others with the mutation and connect them to the support group.

As they make progress, Prof. Russel begins to understand the true meaning of identity. He realizes that our genetic makeup is just one aspect of who we are, and that the connections we form with others and the experiences we go through shape us in profound ways.

INT. SUPPORT GROUP MEETING ROOM - EVENING

Prof. Russel addresses a group of individuals, all carrying the same genetic mutation. He speaks with empathy and understanding, offering them hope and a sense of belonging.

PROF. RUSSEL
You are more than your genetic makeup. Your identity is not defined by this mutation. It is shaped by your experiences, your relationships, and the choices you make. Together, we can face this challenge and create a better future for ourselves and our children.

As the group listens, they begin to share stories, forming bonds that will last a lifetime.

FADE OUT.

End of screenplay.
